decisions.decision: Add a local runtime daemon dry-run loop around adapter replays.
decisions.rationale: This moves FluidGateway from isolated adapter sessions toward a persistent advisory manager loop while preserving the no-mutation boundary.

decisions.decision: Require --state for run-daemon and normalize it before both load and write.
decisions.rationale: The daemon must have an explicit persistence boundary and extensionless state paths must not ignore existing or invalid JSON state.

decisions.decision: Reject daemon --state and --out when they resolve to the same JSON path.
decisions.rationale: State and report writes have different schemas and must not overwrite each other.

decisions.decision: Attach a read-only host capability snapshot to daemon dry-run reports.
decisions.rationale: A future intelligent manager needs CPU, RAM, GPU, and VRAM context before it can make host-aware scheduling or memory-residency decisions.

decisions.decision: Translate host and supervisor evidence into a dry-run daemon decision plan.
decisions.rationale: The project needs a manager-shaped intent layer before any native scheduler or RAM/VRAM residency action can be considered.

decisions.decision: Map daemon decisions into backend-shaped dry-run action queue entries.
decisions.rationale: A future native manager needs concrete CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM action envelopes with safety status, backend requirements, and expected signals.

decisions.decision: Execute queued daemon actions only through an advisory/read-only dry-run executor.
decisions.rationale: The manager loop needs an execution contract now, while native scheduler, memory, GPU, VRAM, and privileged actions must remain blocked until a real backend and safety review exist.

decisions.decision: Convert daemon action execution results into explicit native backend capability and safety requirements.
decisions.rationale: Before a future manager can control CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM, the project needs a testable contract for missing native backends, privilege gates, and safety-review blockers.

decisions.decision: Rank daemon decision lanes with pressure-aware advisory arbitration before native control exists.
decisions.rationale: An intelligent gateway needs a deterministic manager layer that chooses between telemetry, memory, GPU, scheduler, and safety lanes using evidence and preflight blockers.

decisions.decision: Map arbitrated daemon lanes to advisory control intents for CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM-related surfaces.
decisions.rationale: The future gateway needs a stable control-surface contract before any native backend can safely alter scheduler, memory residency, GPU queues, or telemetry behavior.

decisions.decision: Evaluate daemon control intents through an advisory/read-only dry-run executor.
decisions.rationale: The manager needs simulated execution results for each control surface before any future native backend can safely apply CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM changes.

decisions.decision: Declare the backend load contract for every daemon control execution step.
decisions.rationale: A future native manager needs a stable manifest that separates read-only/advisory-ready surfaces from RAM/VRAM/GPU/native surfaces blocked by backend, privilege, and safety-review requirements.

decisions.decision: Execute manifest-approved read-only/advisory probes against existing daemon and host evidence.
decisions.rationale: The gateway needs a concrete proof path from backend contract to CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM signals while native or privileged host control remains blocked.
